Milfe, a port... remote, rich in marine, mining,

First temporary overflow line.
Second temporary overflow line.
Third temporary overflow line.
Fourth temporary overflow line.
Fifth temporary overflow line.
Also thrives as trade hub, independent city.
I arrived at this town, our journey's destination,
I stopped as I entered the central plaza.
Our ship to this town ran aground,
Walking overland, my body felt at the destination
a pleasant fatigue from the relief of arrival.
I rarely tire, so this new sensation felt good.
Feeling odd, I opened my collar and peeked.
I am a man, but there, though faint, is
a bulge that a man should not have.
(I had forgotten...
I should not overdo it...)
I chide myself of this bodily change from fatigue.
We finally arrived, Master.
At that, I closed my shirt, looked up, turned.
A girl with a large pack looks up at me.
Her name is Shuri. For various reasons,
she is my live-in servant, along for this journey.
She was orphaned by war; I took her in.
Since then, she has worked as a servant at home,
mainly taking care of my personal needs.
Having worked here since childhood among servants,
she is especially obedient, devoted, and capable,
Lately, she has become more calm with age,
she keeps her distance now, which makes me lonely.
Is something wrong, Master?
No, it's nothing...
Shuri is staring at me.
That anxious look is the same as when I found her
on the battlefield a decade ago, it's unchanged.
What are your orders now, Master?
Right... Let's get a room first.
Yes, I hope we can find a good inn.
Yeah.
A sudden killing intent pierces me.
I turn toward the killing intent, from an inn.
Familiar figure, shoulders squared, strides near.
That's...
Even so, we are three days late,
I hope Levia isn't angry...
Shuri, unaware of killing intent, notices nothing,
I answer her words with a sigh.
No, she's angry.
Huh?
Of course.
Ah, Levia!
At the sharp voice from behind, Shuri steps aside,
She bowed her head.
With several soldiers, a woman in silver armor
glared as if to kill me.
This woman is General Levia, my current commander
as a guest. She is Lewinia's only female
knight commander, and an old acquaintance.
We were to meet here three days ago, but...
Levia seems very angry.
Celica, what have you been doing all this time?
Levia steps into the space Shuri opened.
The ship ran aground.
What?
It didn't sink, so we walked here.
Shuri, is that true?
Yes, Lady Levia.
Five days ago, our ship ran aground.
Shuri answered as if to defend me. Levia, who
came to my house often, knows Shuri cannot lie.
She nodded slowly.
If Shuri says so, it must be true, but
Then why did you walk?
You could borrow a horse or carriage in a village.
I hesitated for a moment...
True, I could have borrowed a carriage, but
But for a certain reason, I didn't.
She'll be angry...
My gaze meets Shuri's confused eyes.
Even if I lied to cover it, Shuri can't lie,
which is exaggerated, but she is bad at lying, and
I would incur Levia's further wrath...
No choice, so I decided to tell the reason.
The scenery was good...
For a moment, the air seemed to freeze.
Shuri's head, as if about to be loosed at me,
cowers under Levia's anger.
...So you say you walked here?
Yeah.
To the question in a piercingly cold voice,
Levia's brows shoot up at my honest answer.
What do you take this mission for?!
At Levia's furious shout, the people around
cower in fear.
We're searching for missing Princess Ratina right?
Not that, but the meaning of this mission.
A princess, fourth in line, missing for 18 years.
Even if found, she's no use for political marriage
I think...
You... This mission is to redeem war disgrace.
A vital mission entrusted to us by Water Maiden.
Disgrace...
In Levia's homeland, as a guest commander,
a war erupted between Lewinia and a neighbor.
Then, Levia's White Earth Dragon Knights and I
were about to hit the capital from another flank,
fought the enemy's trump card, a giant demon,
and destroyed it despite heavy losses.
However, unlike us who actually fought the demon,
those who only saw its corpse, ignorant nobles,
that Levia, who lost many men, had poor command,
it was said...
Due to wounds from that battle I lost much power,
I was unable to fight in later battles,
and was dismissed as completely useless.
The only one who fairly judged our deeds was
the great guardian god of Lewinia and my ally,
the Water Maiden alone.
Enshrined as a living god deep in the palace,
gave us this mission as oracle to let us recover
and got us out of the postwar chaos at home.
But it seems that didn't get through to Levia,
and she's overly eager.
Even the rumor behind this mission,
that a princess missing 18 years was seen here,
is a dubious rumor.
Even if those nobles don't acknowledge it,
we alone defeated a monster that matched an army,
that's hardly a disgrace worth redeeming.
You're the one who killed that monster.
I couldn't have done it alone.
Shut up! You're the one who finished it.
I... I let my soldiers die in vain...
Levia... the lives lost in battle
calling them wasted doesn't sit well with me.
Ah... sorry, forget what I just said.
Yeah.
Embarrassed by her own words, her anger faded,
Levia turned on her heel as if to hide her face.
For now, I'll brief you on the findings.
Come with me.
Where to?
As Levia turned, Shuri, though loaded with bags,
reached out to take the bags I was holding as well
I dodged Shuri and asked casually.
The vague answer I got was unexpected.
I commandeered the lord's mansion for search HQ.
Levia hates commandeering and looting most.
Moreover, Milfe--visited for the princess search--
is not Lewinian territory; it could be seen as
an invasion.
What happened?
From beside the silent Levia, a man stepped out.
Lord Celica, that was by knights who admire Levia
It was carried out by some common-born knights.
Lord Ranzabu--vice-commander of Levia's knights,
he is a man with many dark rumors.
They wanted General Levia to work in comfort,
but they went overboard, it seems.
Ranzabu shook his head, feigning distress.
We paid the lord of this town a proper sum
and arranged to rent the mansion.
Because those common knights lacked consideration,
we are treated as invaders in this town.
Indeed, in the eyes of the watching townspeople,
there is little goodwill.
Enough, Lord Ranzabu. It's all settled...
Yes, that is true.
I overstepped and spoke presumptuously.
Please forgive me.
In Ranzabu's words,
there was a note of blame toward Levia.
A snake in the grass...
This Ranzabu--he was promoted by nobles who resent
the fact that Levia is a female general.
I hear.
Probably the knights who admired Levia,
Ranzabu likely had a hand in it.
Ranzabu bowed politely to Levia as she turned,
then resumed his position behind Levia.
So, you're going to that mansion now?
Yeah.
Then go ahead, I'll find us an inn.
If that's the case...
No, you're right. Understood...
Levia briefly looks wounded, then turns away.
She shows a slightly dejected expression,
then in the next moment, she leaves.
I understand what Levia wanted to say.
They probably have rooms prepared for us there.
But sorry, Levia, I'd rather not get
dragged into needless trouble.
Because Levia understands that as well,
she left without saying anything.
Shuri stares intently at Levia leaving.
Miss Levia...
Levia, though a woman, holds the rank of general,
and always shoulders needless trouble for it.
Shuri, ignorant of the military, cannot grasp
and that reminds her of her own powerlessness.
On Shuri's face watching Levia leave,
a look of concern for her appears.
So much for a slow recovery.
It's fine...
Master?
You're right.
Though my words were few, that one line
seems to have eased Shuri's anxiety a bit.
Shuri turns back to me, waiting for my words.
Let's find an inn for now.
Ah, yes. Right.
Then I'll look for an inn, Master...
No need. Let's go in there.
Huh?
Shuri turns and sees 'Wild Bull's Hoof Inn' sign.
It looks like a diner at first glance,
but given its size, it seems to be an inn as well.
Seeing me head for the Wild Bull's Hoof Inn,
Shuri hurries ahead, opens the door. I step past.
Savory smell of grilled meat greets me as I enter.
The shop woman
Welcome.
Woman's bright voice greets us as we step inside.
The shop woman
Two of you? That seat is free.
She looks around the nearly full lunchtime shop,
The shop woman at the counter pointed to
two empty seats.
Um, excuse me, is the owner of this shop...?
The shop woman
Being called 'Master' is a bit embarrassing, but
That's me.
Ah, s-sorry!
The shopkeeper
Hehe, you don't have to apologize.
So, what do you need from me?
Ah, no, um, do you have a room available?
The shopkeeper
You're lodging guests? Then come to the counter.
Yes.
When we come to the empty seats at the counter,
Shopkeeper, behind counter, pulls out a ledger.
and turns to face us.
The shopkeeper
I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Rinsha.
And what are your names?
Yes, this is Lord Celica Silfil,
and I am his servant, Shuri.
A servant? Your clothes do show that.
Yes.
Smoothly, Rinsha writes our names into the ledger.
So, a room? A double room is free.
N-no, not at all.
Um, separate rooms...
Rinsha tilts her head at Shuri's fluster.
Oh, really?
Then, adjacent rooms?
Yes, please.
So, how many days are you staying?
Um...
Not decided, but a week for now.
Hearing my voice from behind Shuri,
Rinsha's face shifts to surprise.
Oh, you're a man?
Yeah.
Well, well...
For some reason, I'm often mistaken for a woman.
I am often mistaken for a woman.
Um...
Rinsha stares at my face like it's something rare.
Shuri, looking troubled, calls out to her.
Oh, yes, yes. We require payment upfront, okay?
Yes, how much is it?
Two rooms for a week... 140 shilin.
Shuri's hand freezes opening the money pouch.
What's wrong?
Shilin, you say...?
Yes... Ah! Don't tell me you don't have it?
Yes, we could pay in Rudra until now, so...
Come to think of it, when we left Lewinia, Levia
that the currency used in this town is different.
Oh, in this town you can't use Rudra.
I'll go exchange it.
No way.
Huh?
Three days ago, the Lewinian army came,
and they all exchanged currency, so
the exchange's vault got filled with Rudra.
What!
So yesterday, all the exchange staff,
said they'd go exchange in another town and left.
That's...
I put a hand on the flustered Shuri's shoulder and
stepped forward to Rinsha the innkeeper.
Ah, Master...
Can you pay with this?
I pulled a jewel from my pocket and held it out.
What's this? A jewel?
No wonder she's surprised. It's redder than blood,
The jewel shines clear without a single cloud,
and is larger than her wide-open eyes.
I think it was enough to live idly for a year.
You planning to buy the whole inn?
I have no such intention.
Then... I can't accept such a precious jewel.
Then treat it as a deposit.
A deposit?
If we leave without paying for the room,
you can keep that jewel.
So if I pay, I give the jewel back?
Right.
I see. In that case, forget one week--
stay as long as you like.
Yeah. We'll do that.
Heheh. Then I'll show you to your room.
Rinsha heads for the stairs to the second floor.
Um, Master...
What is it?
Are you sure that was wise?
That jewel from the Water Priestess was very...
Was it?
Yes. If I recall, it was valuable enough to
let someone live in leisure for a lifetime...
Master?
Where are you going, Master?
After Rinsha led me to my room, just in case,
I checked escape routes and finally settled in.
I surveyed the room that will be mine for a while.
The room was bright and clean,
From the second-floor window,
I had a full view of the central plaza.
The cheap inns I stayed at while on the run,
are worlds apart from this room...
Suddenly, memories of those days came back to me.
Decades ago, for certain reasons, in ancient times
I fought a goddess said to have vanished to heaven
Against a goddess of absolute power, miraculously,
I won in a mutual strike and sealed her will,
With my original body fatally wounded,
I survived by taking the goddess's body...
That was... the beginning of everything...
The god I defeated opposed the ruling gods.
Though called a dark god, it was still a god.
Still, the other gods and their followers
feared me as 'God Slayer' and tried to erase me.
Decades on, with goddess's body, I stopped aging.
I fought and fled much of the world for decades.
I allied with Lewinia's only unaffiliated goddess.
I allied with the Water Maiden for brief haven.
In Lewinia, where Water Maiden is state religion,
Other gods and their followers rarely targeted me.
But in this non-Lewinian town, my true identity
if discovered, all townspeople would be my enemies
and I'd be hunted until fleeing back to Lewinia.
The room had a locked chest for luggage and such,
It was clearly a room meant for long stays.
Caught in thought, I suddenly recalled,
and took from my luggage by the bed a sheathed
dagger.
No large ornaments, but smooth female curves and
the tastefully designed dagger, when I held it,
A languid young woman's voice echoed in my head.
(What, have you finally arrived?)
(Yeah.)
I replied to that voice in my mind.
The source of this voice is the dagger I hold,
It's demon Haishera's voice sealed in the dagger.
This one, after I performed the God Slaying,
challenged me to a fight, but
I defeated Haishera and sealed her in that sword.
Since then, Haishera has recognized me as master,
and as a demon sword, she fought battles with me.
But now, after losing power in the war,
if I try to use her, she'd take me over
and our roles would be reversed...
(Still, keeping me packed away in your luggage
is that not a bit too cruel?)
(Sorry, I forgot.)
(You really are something...)
The room has locked chests for luggage.
It looks like a room for long-term stays.

I sheathed Haishera
and looked around the room again.
Hmm, a fine room for a border town.
Seeing the room through my eyes, Haishera
lets out a rare word of praise.
But when Shuri isn't with me, as in this trip,
She means compared to the cheap inns I stay at.
Yeah, it's a nice room.
Hehe, thanks.
I meant to reply to Haishera, but I thoughtlessly
muttered aloud. Rinsha, holding fresh sheets,
was smiling from the doorway.
Now, drop off your bags and invite Shuri
and head to the dining hall. You're hungry, right?

I hadn't noticed until she said it,
but come to think of it,
I haven't eaten since arriving in town.
Is that okay?
Don't worry, I'll put it on your tab.

Then Rinsha took the gem from her chest
and showed it.
Rinsha and I left the upstairs room and went down.
came down.

After that, Shuri came to my room
to check unasked.
seeing the sheets in Rinsha's hands,
offered to clean and make the bed herself.
Rinsha hesitated at first, saying it was too much,
but was overwhelmed by Shuri's pleading manner,
and accepted the offer.
She's an unusual girl...
Shuri's smile when taking the sheets from Rinsha
She must be recalling that cheerful smile,
Rinsha speaks to me with a wry smile.
That girl is the hardest worker in the house.
Oh, you have other servants?
Yeah.
Hmm, having that many servants...
Celica, are you perhaps nobility?
No.
Then, who are you?
Without answering, I sat at a free table.
I sat at a nearby table in the dining hall.
She thought my silence meant I would not talk.
Rinsha silently brought a menu from the counter
and placed it before me.
I guarantee the taste.
Rinsha, beaming, puffed out her ample chest.
She showed off her full chest even more.
The cooking aroma filling the dining hall was
enough to stimulate my appetite.
True...
Something light and small in portion...
You order like a girl... then try this.
Rinsha's finger pointed to a dish on the menu.
I see.
So, Shuri...
She'll be here soon.
No sooner said, Shuri came down the stairs
with quiet yet hurried steps.
Oh, really...
Her quiet, hurried steps when Shuri was a child,
she often used to run up to me,
so I warned her she might fall and get hurt,
and she's walked like this ever since.
I'm sorry for keeping you waiting...
It's fine, right, Celica?
Yeah.
So, Shuri, what will you have?
Ah, I'll have mine after my Master.
Saying that, Shuri stood diagonally behind me.
What's wrong, Shuri?
Rinsha called out to Shuri curiously.
Yes, allow me to serve.
Serve...?
Rinsha's eyes, now dots, turned to me.
Shuri, sit down.
But, Master...
This is the usual exchange...
Whenever we eat out, Shuri always does this.
She tries to volunteer as a server.
If left alone, she'd serve perfectly, but...
At the mansion it's fine, but in a restaurant...
It's extremely conspicuous...
That's right, Shuri. Our food isn't so hard
that you need to stand and serve.
Besides, it'd be sad to make Master eat alone.
Shuri.
Yes, as you wish...
Urged, Shuri finally stepped from behind me...
Shuri's posture as she sat down awkwardly...
It wasn't reluctance, but rather nervousness.
I'll have this.
I looked at Shuri, cheeks flushed and head down,
I pointed to the dish Rinsha recommended.
Yes, and you, Shuri?
Ah, then I'll have the same as Master...
Just Shuri's typical response.
I see, huh.
Rinsha nodded slowly, then
elbowed my back and walked to the kitchen.
Soon after, Rinsha returned with three meals.
I haven't eaten yet. Can I join you?
She said while placing three dishes on the table.
Yeah.
Thanks.
As I answered, she gave a brisk smile,
sat down across from me,
and fired off rapid questions...
So what brought you two to this town?
Recuperation.
Oh, but earlier, by my place with Levia,
weren't you talking?
Does Levia come here often?
Yeah, she's a regular. Just as I thought...
What do you mean?
So the man who never showed up was you, Celica.
Did Levia say that?
Yeah, she was mad: 'What's the mission?'
I was told that already.
Rinsha laughs cheerfully.
So you came to find someone too?
Half is for recovery.
Oh, not so serious?
And Levia works so hard.
Yeah.
Levia is dedicated, but works too hard.
I hope that doesn't backfire.
What do you think of Levia and the others?
Huh? They're customers.
Rinsha answers as if it's obvious.
No, I mean... Levia's impression in this town
doesn't seem good.
Ah, right... are you worried?
Something like that.
Hehe, it's okay. There were some issues
at first, but Levia herself is popular
with the townspeople.
Really?
Yes, even with her title, she's polite to
everyone, and many people look up to her,
especially the girls.
I see...
Since Levia became a general though a woman,
some men resent her, but women love her.
When Levia was at the palace in Lewinia,
she was always surrounded by noble girls,
looking exasperated. I saw that a lot.
But...
What?
Seems the town watch doesn't get along with them.
Town watch?
Yes, the lord hired mercenaries when Levia came,
They're the ones hired for emergencies.
In case of emergency... Levia occupies this town
Is that what you mean?
Yes, I keep telling them Levia wouldn't do that.
But the ones hired under those circumstances
The vigilantes are hostile toward Levia's group.
I see...
After the meal, I ate the last parsley garnish
I popped it into my mouth and stood up.
I'll work enough not to get Levia angry.
Seeing me stand, Shuri, who had already eaten,
also rose and looked at me.
Master
I'll be back by evening. Feel free until then.
Yes, understood.
Following Shuri's prompt reply, Rinsha also stood.
Well, I guess I'll get back to work too.
Saying that, she began clearing the dishes.
Please take care.
I passed through the door past Shuri bowing,
I stepped into the central plaza facing the inn,
From inside, I could hear Shuri's voice.
Miss Rinsha, please let me help...
(Oh dear, such a diligent girl...)
